hints: Start at the beginning of the story. Which molecules have just arrived from the link reaction and Krebs cycle carrying hydrogen to the mitochondrion?
When electrons release energy as they move down the carriers, protons are pumped across a membrane. Think about which small compartment between the two mitochondrial membranes fills up with protons.
A gradient only exists across something. Recall the highly folded membrane where the electron carriers and proton pumps are actually embedded.
Protons are now concentrated on one side and cannot pass through the lipid bilayer. Think about what type of passive movement they use to rush back down their concentration gradient.
The channel that lets protons back into the matrix is also the enzyme that makes ATP from ADP and phosphate. Recall its name.
At the very end, electrons must be removed or the chain blocks. Think about which element acts as the final acceptor and joins with protons and electrons to make water.
walkthrough:
Reduced Coenzymes Supply the Hydrogen**
Reduced NAD and reduced FAD are made in glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle. Here they are oxidised, releasing hydrogen atoms to the first carriers of the electron transport chain. That is why the first gap is NAD / FAD.

Electrons Drive Proton Pumping**
Each hydrogen splits into a proton ($H^+$) and an electron. Electrons are passed from carrier to carrier, losing energy at each step. That energy is used to actively pump protons from the matrix across the inner membrane into the intermembrane space. So the second gap is intermembrane space.

A Gradient Across the Inner Membrane**
The pumps and cytochrome carriers sit in the inner mitochondrial membrane, folded into cristae to give a large surface area. Pumping creates a higher concentration of protons in the intermembrane space than in the matrix, so the gradient is across the cristae / inner membrane. That is the third gap.

Chemiosmosis Back Into the Matrix**
The inner membrane is impermeable to protons, so they can only return to the matrix down their electrochemical gradient through a specific protein channel. This passive movement down a gradient is diffusion. So the fourth gap is diffuse.

ATP Synthase Makes ATP**
The channel protein is ATP synthase, also called ATP synthetase or stalked particle. As protons flow through it, the energy of the gradient drives the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate ($ADP + Pi \rightarrow ATP$). That is the fifth gap.

Oxygen Clears the Electrons**
At the end of the chain, electrons combine with protons and oxygen to form water ($2H^+ + 2e^- + 1/2O_2 \rightarrow H_2O$). Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, which is why aerobic respiration needs a continuous supply of oxygen. So the last gap is oxygen.

Final answer: Reduced NAD / FAD releases hydrogen atoms to cytochrome carriers. Energy from electron transfer is used to pump protons into the intermembrane space, so that a proton gradient is set up across the cristae / inner membrane. Protons diffuse through the channel protein known as ATP synthase, into the matrix, producing ATP. The protons combine with electrons and oxygen atoms to form water.
